html:
SMTO-PRL-0007 — These steps can't run together this way

GUID: 86d60733-c1c4-45b7-84af-dc3c4b6f86a8
Slug: parallel-foreground-required
Domain: PRL · Subsystem: prl

What happened

  • SMTO tried to run a group of steps in a way groups don't support, such as running in the background, needing typed input, or needing administrator (sudo) access. None of them were started.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. If a step needs you to type something, or needs administrator (sudo) access, ask SMTO to run that step by itself, not as part of a group. Grouped steps run without a terminal or typed input, so these steps have to run alone.
  2. If long work should keep running in the background, open Agent Checks, choose This run, and turn on Background activities. SMTO only runs steps in the background when Background activities is on for the task.
  3. To make that the default for future tasks, turn on Background activities in Settings › Operate › Asynchronous task execution. New tasks then start with background work allowed.

What success looks like

  • The steps start and appear in the Activities section, each with its own result.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't treat this message as a sign the steps ran; none of them were started.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Activity preflight rejected the batch (parallel_foreground_required): it asked for background mode while background activities are off, non-captured or interactive execution, or terminal, stdin or job context; shell sequences also reject privileged (sudo) or terminal-input context.

What this means

  • Preflight rejects a disallowed background mode, uncaptured/interactive execution or task-owned terminal/stdin/job context; shell sequences also reject incompatible privileged/terminal input context. Activity ownership, preflight and durable receipts determine admission and effect certainty. Rejected new work does not erase prior child effects; recovery and diagnostics never replay an unknown operation.

Why this can happen

  • Preflight rejects a disallowed background mode, uncaptured/interactive execution or task-owned terminal/stdin/job context; shell sequences also reject incompatible privileged/terminal input context.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect effective background/resource policy and the actual execution envelope; supported background exceptions depend on that path.

How to fix it

  • Run grouped items in captured, non-interactive foreground mode. Route interactive, terminal, stdin or sudo commands through a single shell.command, and enable Background activities for the run (Agent Checks, This run) or globally (Settings › Operate › Asynchronous task execution) when background mode is intended.
  • Use the captured non-interactive mode required by this path, or route terminal/background work through its supported ordinary controls.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • Each operation uses the mode supported by its current activity path and passes ordinary admission.

What not to do

  • Do not bypass the unsupported-feature check or reinterpret an unsupported response as success.

Technical notes

  • Activity ownership, preflight and durable receipts determine admission and effect certainty. Rejected new work does not erase prior child effects; recovery and diagnostics never replay an unknown operation.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
